description: The previous code used Option<HashSet> as a workaround to extend a locally-constructed HashSet's lifetime into a match arm, then called .as_ref().unwrap() to recover a reference. The unwrap() could not panic (the None arm always populated the Option before taking the reference), but a reader had no way to verify this without reading the entire block. The new form names the HashSet directly in the outer scope and takes &on_demand in the None arm. This is the canonical Rust pattern for lifetime extension across match arms: bind the owned value before the match so its lifetime covers all arms, take a reference inside the arm that needs it. A contributor might suggest reverting to the Option pattern (thinking the unwrap makes the initialization explicit), but the Option wrapper was purely a lifetime workaround — it added a fallible-looking call with no actual fallibility. The new form is both cleaner and more honest about the control flow.
title: on_demand borrow dance: owned value in outer scope, reference in match arm — idiomatic Rust lifetime extension
